anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as SaaS subscription data (MRR, ARR, paying customers, new MRR, churned MRR, logo churn). MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. A customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure. The cancellation date in this export is when a customer asked to cancel, not when the subscription ended: a subscription keeps paying until its end date (or a scheduled cancellation date). Some subscriptions are scheduled to cancel after the latest date: they are still paying and are counted until they end. On a subscription list, MRR is computed by the product from each subscription's price, seats, discount and billing interval, at today's price: expansion, contraction and revenue retention need monthly MRR snapshots and are not computed from it.

executive_view.headline: MRR stands at $869,234.95 as of 29 Oct 2026, up from $787,836.74 a year earlier, while logo churn has risen to 18.8% from 13.7% over the same period.

findings.text: Logo churn reached 18.8% in the 12-month cohort to 29 Oct 2026, up from 13.7% in the cohort to 29 Oct 2025, a rise of 5.1 points.
Enterprise accounts for $631,048.45 of total MRR, while Mid contributes $112,997.17 and SMB $125,189.33.
February 2026 saw churned MRR of $57,995.65 against a usual month of $4,888.70, with 45% of that spike attributable to a single Enterprise customer.
MRR per customer varies widely — the median is $845.75 while the mean is $3,160.73, ranging from $31.24 to $47,940.00 — reflecting the concentration of value in a small number of large accounts.
Total mrr: Enterprise (631,048.45) is higher than SMB (125,189.33).
Total mrr: Enterprise (631,048.45) is higher than Mid (112,997.16).

evidence.claim: The file's story in the product's own numbers: Logo churn (12-month cohort to 29 Oct 2026): 18.8%; a year earlier (12-month cohort to 29 Oct 2025): 13.7%, +5.1 points. MRR bridge, 12 months to 29 Oct 2026: $787,836.74 on 29 Oct 2025 + new MRR $276,080.10 + reactivation MRR $12,029.90 − churned MRR $206,513.79 − net expansion less contraction (not split in this file) $198.00 = $869,234.95. This file has no monthly values per customer, so expansion and contraction are not split. 73 customers left at a month-end in the window (churned customers); logo churn counts only the customers in force on 29 Oct 2025 who are not in force now, so the two differ: customers who joined in the window or came back are in the count only. The largest month of churned MRR: Feb 2026 with $57,995.65 (a usual month: $4,888.70), 45% of it one customer_id in Enterprise (segment). 479 rows are 437 customers (42 with more than one row); 251 in force at 29 Oct 2026. 1 start or end date falls after 29 Oct 2026: not counted yet. 10 rows are paused or unpaid today: a subscription list holds its status for today only, with no date it began, so they are out of every month-end's MRR, never churned at a guessed date. 5 rows have an ended status but no end date.
